input: Create a digital inventory of home valuables for insurance

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The inventory could cover everything in the home or be limited to high-value categories (jewelry, electronics, art, furniture) — this changes how much work is involved and what detail is needed.
Whether this is for a single person, a couple, or a whole household affects whose items are included and who needs access to the final document.
The number of rooms and size of the home directly determines the scale of the project and how it should be broken down into manageable steps.
A hard deadline (e.g., upcoming policy renewal) or a time budget per session shapes how quickly the inventory must be completed and how detailed each entry can be.
The chosen tool — spreadsheet, dedicated app, cloud document — determines the format, accessibility, and how photos or receipts get attached.
The level of detail per item (photo, serial number, purchase receipt, estimated value) affects both effort and the inventory's usefulness during a real claim.
Knowing whether the goal is to satisfy a specific insurer's requirements, get a personal record, or prepare for a policy upgrade changes what 'done' looks like.

gold.taskTitle: Create home valuables inventory for insurance
gold.taskDescription: Build a digital record of household valuable items to support insurance coverage, claims, or policy reviews.

questions.title: Which categories of items are you focusing on?
questions.description: Is this a full room-by-room sweep of everything, or focused on specific high-value categories like jewelry, electronics, art, or appliances?

questions.title: How many rooms or properties need to be covered?
questions.description: Understanding the physical scale — number of rooms, outbuildings, or multiple properties — determines how to break the work into sessions.

questions.title: Is there a deadline driving this, like a policy renewal?
questions.description: A hard date or time constraint will shape how quickly the inventory must be completed and how much detail is realistic to capture.

questions.title: What tool do you want to store the inventory in?
questions.description: For example: a spreadsheet (Excel, Google Sheets), a dedicated home inventory app, a shared cloud document, or something your insurer provides.

questions.title: How much detail do you want to capture per item?
questions.description: Options range from a basic description and value estimate, up to serial numbers, purchase receipts, photos, and appraisal documents.

questions.title: Who else needs access to this inventory?
questions.description: Should the document be shared with a partner, a family member, or directly with your insurance provider — or is it just for your own records?

questions.title: What does your insurer specifically require for a valid claim?
questions.description: Do you have guidance from your insurance company on required fields, formats, or proof of value, or is this a self-directed record with no external spec?
